purpose: Replace the remaining industrial supply cart, rails and powered winch with a documented period delivery presentation.
candidate: Straight-box freight wagon, with a carefully sourced Murphy-type interpretation; no manufacturer logo or claim of an exact surviving vehicle yet.

sources.title: NPS, Wagons on the Emigrant Trails
sources.consulted: Article and linked Murphy replica photograph inspected.
sources.claims: Murphy wagons used straight boxes, with a roughly12ft bed and9ft overall height; contrasted with the curved Conestoga. The illustrated Murphy wagon was built in1979, so it is a modern reconstruction rather than a period photograph.
sources.observations: Larger rear wheels, smaller front wheels, wooden spokes and hubs, narrow iron tires, a straight board box and tied canvas over bows. Display ageing is not colour direction.

sources.title: NPS, Transportation on the Santa Fe Trail
sources.claims: Freight wagons varied. The article reproduces an1858 description of heavy wagons with64in rear wheels and13ft tongues; those dimensions are not automatically Murphy dimensions. The loading-dock image is explicitly undated.
sources.observations: Large spoked rear wheels, smaller front wheels, open wagon bows and hanging running-gear fittings. Monochrome photo does not establish paint colours; do not reproduce the pictured people without individual historical treatment.

sources.title: NPS/Montana SHPO, Whoop-Up Trail documentation,1991
sources.consulted: Previously sourced in art/action_props/whiskey-kit-evidence.json S24; not freshly re-read in this pass.
sources.candidate_claim: Existing research records Murphy wagon red running gear, blue box and white top. Re-read the relevant passage and its citations before rendering.
